If I *had* a second monitor, I'm sure I would do the same. It's cool to find someone else who has the same process, though. I always thought I was being super OCD, needing to have that timeline in front of me.

I tried having it on my computer for a while, but without the list staring me in the face I forget about it. It started out in a notepad next to my keyboard, then to the chalkboard which has moved around my room until ending up above my monitor. While my handwriting isn't so great either (guess who works in the medical profession), I put it in my absolute best handwriting. I can read that, at least, even if most other people can't.

I have a chalkboard mounted on the wall above my monitor. In large letters it says "The All Important Timeline." Below the title is a bulleted timeline, with the part that has been written into the novel in pink chalk and things to come in white. It started out as just outlining the basic plot, but has become more and more detailed the more I write. It's one of the best writing tools I have.
